topics.name: Arduino Mega 2560
topics.question: What is the Arduino Mega 2560 and what are its limits
topics.assetAlt: Official Arduino Mega 2560 Rev3 pinout diagram, colour-coding the power pins, the sixteen analog inputs A0–A15, PWM-capable digital pins, the four serial ports, and the microcontroller port names.

sections.heading: What it offers
paragraphs: The Mega gives 54 digital I/O pins (15 PWM-capable), 16 analog inputs with a 10-bit ADC (0–1023), and multiple hardware serial ports. It is the hub every sensor and actuator connects to.

sections.heading: Logic levels
paragraphs: It runs 5 V logic. Analog reads return 0–1023 across 0–5 V; digital writes are a clean 0 V / 5 V. Respect the ≈20 mA per-pin limit and never back-power motors through the board.

topics.hint: A board that resets or behaves randomly when a motor runs is being overdrawn — power actuators from a separate supply and tie the grounds together.

topics.name: LMC6484 Op-Amp
topics.question: What is the LMC6484, and why a rail-to-rail single-supply part
topics.assetAlt: LMC6484 quad op-amp pinout: a 14-pin package containing four amplifiers, showing each amplifier’s inverting input, non-inverting input and output, plus the shared V+ and V− supply pins.

sections.heading: Why this part
paragraphs: The LMC6484 packs four CMOS op-amps with rail-to-rail input and output, running from a single supply — ideal for 5 V Arduino projects where signals live close to ground or the rail.

sections.heading: Using it well
paragraphs: Add a decoupling capacitor near the supply pins, mind the pinout when wiring all four amplifiers, and remember the output still cannot quite reach the rails under load.

topics.hint: An amplifier output that cannot reach the value you expect near 0 V or 5 V is losing headroom under load — lower the gain or bias the signal away from the rails.
